🟢 **F-1397-3 (s1397, MEASURED) — `citation-title-guard`'s quote extraction desynchronises on short inline-code spans, so a correct citation can red for reasons in the prose beside it.** Its `QUOTED` regex treats every backtick, straight quote **and apostrophe** as a delimiter and requires 12–160 characters between a pair, so **an unpaired quote character shifts the pairing for everything after it**. Two triggers were measured, both in ordinary prose: an inline-code span shorter than 12 characters (skipped as an opener), and — caught only when this very row first reddened the guard — **a possessive apostrophe, as in "E1's", which is an unpaired delimiter the writer never thinks of as one.** In both cases — the regex then captures the prose *between* code spans instead of the spans themselves. Measured: a verbatim quote of a real source line sat inside the window and was never extracted, because a nearby 9-character span had offset the pairing. Two neighbours worth knowing: the window is ±400 characters, so a citation's verdict can depend on where that window happens to start; and `MIN_PREFIX` is 20, so a 19-character quoted prefix fails. **NOT filed as a defect to fix** — the guard's purpose (recoverability) is served and loosening the regex risks false greens. **Recorded as a cure for the next reader:** put the quote immediately after the citation, in double quotes, with no inline-code spans between them. **GATE: none — informational.**

Now that 2D is cheap, the honest readings of the same intent diverge: **(a) RE-BASELINE to the absolute budget** — drop the ratio assertion and keep the frame-budget one, on the grounds that what protects the player is ms-per-frame, not a comparison against a renderer being retired; **(b) KEEP the ratio and treat ~1.4–1.6 as a real 3D perf target**, i.e. accept that the 3D path is now the expensive one and book optimisation work; **(c) re-baseline the RATIO to a measured multiple** (say 2.0) so it still catches regressions without asserting parity that no longer holds. ➡️ **Recommendation (c) then (a): keep a ratio gate — it is the only thing that would catch a genuine 3D regression — but re-baseline it against measured current values and state the baseline date in the test.** A bar nobody can meet gets muted, and a muted gate catches nothing. ⓘ **Filed rather than fixed because choosing what a gate should ASSERT is a design act, not a drain act**, and because the number to re-baseline to should be measured on an idle machine (my readings carry a live Codex job in the background). Run 2, same commit, stock playwright-managed `npm run dev` and a now-warm dep cache → painted **11.0** ms, terrain3d 16.9, ratio **1.54**, test **FAILED in 19.5 s**. **The whole test got 4× faster on the second run**, which is the tell: vite`s dependency pre-bundling (`Re-optimizing dependencies because vite config has changed`, logged at server start) taxes the early boots, and this spec measures the PAINTED arm first in every contract. The tax therefore lands mostly on the denominator and drags the ratio down under the bar. ⚠️ **I nearly reported that green as a refutation of the predecessor finding** — a fire before me had a red, I had a green on the same tree, and the tempting story was "not reproducible". It was reproducible; my instrument was cold. ➡️ **Rule for any future p95/perf measurement: discard the first run against a newly-created worktree or a newly-started dev server, or warm it with a throwaway run first.** A cheap tell is wall-clock — if the run takes multiples of its usual time, the numbers in it are not comparable to anything. ⓘ The bisect that produced the predecessor row was run AFTER the cache was warm and re-used one server generation throughout, and its boundary was confirmed by two independent passes, so it is not affected. 💡 **The class: a warm-up artefact does not add noise, it adds BIAS — and bias that flatters your hypothesis is the kind you stop looking for.**

🟡 **F-1347-1 (s1347, MEASURED + PATCHED — A THIRD OF THE EVIDENCE THE OPEN ROWS POINT AT WAS NEVER SEARCHED, BECAUSE THE LEDGER CITES FILES BY BARE BASENAME).** `scripts/row-quote-currency.mjs` scores each quote against the union of the row's READABLE paths, and a cited token was readable only when it was an exact repo-relative path on disk. ✓ **MEASURED on the live board: 46 of 136 citations on open rows (34%) resolved to NOTHING** — `fire.md`, `Game.ts`, `goals.json`, `lane-usable.mjs`, `lane-runner-v3.sh` — **and 31 of those 46 named exactly one tracked file.** A row citing one resolvable path beside three basenames had its quotes searched in a quarter of the evidence it actually pointed at, and the systematic direction of that error is **FALSE ABSENT** — the interesting-looking answer, exactly the shape F-1346-2 warns about. 🔒 **PATCHED (`f6af7eae`):** resolution is exact > unique-tail > unique-basename; **AMBIGUOUS and unknown stay UNREADABLE and are reported as such**, because guessing a file manufactures false PRESENT as readily as false ABSENT, and a false PRESENT is worse — it retires a row that is still live. (`Game.ts` is ambiguous with `.s195-probe-bak/Game.ts`; 16 files share `RUN-NOTE.md`. The tail rule splits `production-newsie-mei/RUN-NOTE.md` and correctly REFUSES `hero/RUN-NOTE.md`.) ⚠️ **AND THE RESULT REFUTED MY OWN PREDICTION, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH INHERITING — see F-1347-3.** Self-test 20/20 with manufactured-defect controls asserting BOTH directions. **GATE: none — closed by the patch; kept open only as the record of the measurement.**

🟡 **F-1347-2 (s1347, MEASURED + PATCHED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT OVERSOLD — THE QUOTER'S TERMINAL PUNCTUATION IS NOT THE QUOTED FILE'S).** Found by hand, not by the instrument: `tasks/BACKLOG.md:381` (F-1289-1) quotes *"the status word is the ONLY thing that can refuse a re-queue."* and the probe called it GONE, while `scripts/goal-tracker.test.mjs:47` reads *"...refuse a re-queue, and while"* — the row appended a period to close its own sentence. 🔒 **PATCHED (`f6af7eae`)**: terminal `[.,;:!?]` relaxed as a FALLBACK only, so an exact hit always wins, and the relaxed needle can never match MORE text than the exact one. 📏 **HONEST SIZE, stated because a fixed class invites over-reading: this rescues 1 of 38 live ABSENT quotes.** It was fixed because it is correct and free, **not** because it moved the board — and the census that measured it (`archive/scratch/s1347-punctuation-census.mjs`) is in git so nobody re-derives the 1/38. **GATE: none — closed by the patch.**

I FIXED THE LARGEST GAP AND IT BOUGHT SIX MORE WRONG ANSWERS).** s1346 read 28 of 61 open rows as UNRESOLVED and named that bucket *the real remaining gap*. F-1347-1 fixed the largest reason rows land there, and I predicted it would clear false ABSENTs. ✗ **ZERO rows flipped ABSENT → PRESENT** (per-row transition diff, `archive/scratch/s1347-verdict-diff.mjs`, both readers on the same rows). What it did instead: **6 rows moved UNRESOLVED → ABSENT, and I read all six at source — ALL SIX ARE FALSE ABSENTS.** F-1305-3 quotes **another ROW** (s1303's words) beside a spec-file citation · F-1319-1 quotes a **TEMPLATE**, `✅ **SHIPPED sNNNN at <hash>**`, which is verbatim in no file *by construction* · F-1322-2 and F-1289-1 quote **commands** · F-1084-3 quotes **test-log output** · F-1343-2's `src e2e functions scripts` is an **ENUMERATION**, not a quotation. ➡️ **THE CLASS: this probe cannot distinguish "text I am quoting FROM the cited file" from "text I am proposing, commanding, templating, or narrating" — and the ledger writes far more of the latter inside backticks. 🟡 **F-1346-1 (s1346, MEASURED — s1345 §H(3) ASKED FOR A PROBE FOR ROWS WHOSE SUBJECT IS A *DOCUMENT*; IT IS BUILT, AND ITS FIRST RESULT IS THAT MOST OPEN ROWS ARE NOT PROBEABLE AT ALL).** s1345 cleared the five cheapest CODE-subject rows with `git log` plus a read, then named the gap: the remainder argue about a guard's source, a law surface, an inventory or a master, and *"those need a different probe than `git log`, and nobody has designed one."* ✓ **BUILT: `scripts/row-quote-currency.mjs`.** These rows are unusually quotable — they cite a path and then quote the exact sentence they are arguing about — so the probe asks one question per quote: **does that verbatim string still occur in a file the row names?** Proximity to a path citation decides *whether* a quote is checkable; the union of every path the row names decides the *verdict* (both halves were measured necessary — see F-1346-2). 📊 **LIVE RESULT, and the headline is the denominator, not the hit rate: of 61 open rows, 28 offer NOTHING checkable and only 41 quotes across 33 rows can be asked at all.** Of those 41, **15 present / 26 gone**; rows rank ABSENT 20 / PRESENT 13 / UNRESOLVED 28. ⚠️ **ABSENT RANKS A ROW FOR PROBING — IT IS NOT A CLOSURE AND NOT A DEFECT**, and I am naming the three false-positive classes I measured rather than leaving them for the next reader to rediscover: a quoted line later **EXTENDED** (F-1336-2 — `AP-08 — THE ALPHA EXCHANGE + THE COUNTY FAIR` is alive and well in the spec; a `; lineage: …` was appended after the row quoted it), a **shell command** quoted as evidence (F-1336-3), and a quote of **another ROW** rather than a file. ⚖️ **AND ABSENCE HAS NO DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE LIMIT THAT MATTERS:** a row may quote text asserting what IS in a file (gone ⇒ premise rotted) or the text it says is MISSING and ought to be added (gone ⇒ the row is still LIVE). F-1284-1 is the second kind — `"Bash(bash scripts/deploy.sh)"` is genuinely absent from the settings file, and that absence is the finding, not its expiry. **A verdict still requires reading the row.** ⓘ Also worth the next fire's minute: a row is flagged if **any one** of its quotes is gone, so output is sorted by the FRACTION gone — **F-1305-1 and F-1345-1 both flag ABSENT while the sentence each is actually arguing about is still in place** (I grepped both). **GATE: none — the instrument is committed and self-tested. When a process cannot perform an act, give it somewhere to put the act; otherwise the only container left is the handoff, and a handoff is read once by one successor who has its own priorities.*

🔺 **F-1349-2 (s1349, HAZARD — OPENED WITH ITS CURE, NO OWNER ACTION NEEDED: THE `attended-owed` MECHANISM HAD NO RULE AGAINST LANDING AN ITEM BY ROUTING AROUND THE DENIAL THAT CREATED IT).** Neither `tasks/attended-owed/README.md` nor `scripts/attended-owed-audit.mjs` said anything about *how not to* clear an item. ⚠️ **And the gap is live, not theoretical: `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(cat:*)`, `Bash(cp:*)` and `Bash(mv:*)` are all on the fire allowlist** (`.claude/settings.json`), so a fire almost certainly **could** write a `.claude/` target from a shell. **I did not attempt it, and that refusal is the finding's point** — the boundary on `.claude/` exists to stop an autonomous agent editing its own instruction surface, and an agent that complies with one tool and defeats it with another has defeated the control, not honoured it. **The denial is the answer, not an obstacle in front of the answer.** 🎯 **The predictable failure mode is ATTRITION, not ignorance.** These items are by construction cheap, already-decided, fully composed, and re-read at every single fire; item 001 has now been printed **seven** times without landing. The fire most likely to shell around it is a **late** one carrying six predecessors' frustration — so the warning is aimed at that exact moment and says so in those words. ✅ **CURED IN THE SAME COMMIT, at the two surfaces that are actually read:** the class-level rule now heads `tasks/attended-owed/README.md` (read when an item is *opened*), and the per-item `why:` line — **the string the audit prints at every fire** — now ends *"Do NOT shell around it."* 🚫 **Deliberately NOT propagated to `scripts/fire.md`:** the audit's printed line already reaches every fire on the read path, and this corpus's larger standing problem is over-propagation, not under-. 💡 **REUSABLE SHAPE:** a queue built to hold work a process is *forbidden* to do is a standing invitation to do it another way — **whenever you build one, write the anti-bypass rule at the same time**, because the person who needs it is not the person who built it.

✅ **F-1342-2 (s1342, MEASURED — AN OWNER-DESK BUG REPORT DESCRIBES A DEFECT THAT ITS OWN CITED SCREENSHOT REFUTES; IT HAD BEEN CARRIED SINCE s1257).** Running s1341 §I(2)'s currency sweep I (`:1013–1017`), so a truncated name would render **`the Prospect…`** — the cited PNG shows **`the Prospector` complete, no ellipsis**. ✓ **No repair could have masked this**: `src/styles.css` last moved `52fa15ad` (2026-07-26) and `src/ui/Hud.ts` `e5bd6260` (2026-07-22) — **both untouched since before F-1257-4 was written.** 🔑 **THE CLASS, AND IT IS THE COMPLEMENT OF THIS REPO'S USUAL FAILURE.** The house law is *evidence, not vibes* — and F-1257-4 **had** evidence: a real screenshot, from a real plain boot, at the right viewport. **It was read like prose instead of like a DOM.** Three adjacent inline elements in one visual line are indistinguishable from one wrapped string **to the eye**, and a glyph rendered small in a serif face is ambiguous **to the eye** — so a screenshot is a rich source about *appearance* and a **near-worthless one about STRUCTURE**, which is exactly what a "clipping" claim is about. ⚠️ **The cost is asymmetric and it is why this is a finding rather than a shrug: a false NEGATIVE from a screenshot wastes nobody's time, but a false POSITIVE mints an owner action** — and this one sat on the desk for **85 fires**, re-listed every handoff, asking overlapping, mis-aligned — the screenshot is the SYMPTOM and the DOM is the EVIDENCE; a bug report that never left the image is a description of your own eyesight. **Cheap discriminator: ask what the defect would have looked like if it were real.** Here it would have carried an ellipsis, and it did not.*

these are 7,000–16,000. **And the loss is invisible from inside the fire that causes it** — the fire replaced line-1 on purpose, its commit looks correct, and the victim is always a *successor* reading a board that no longer mentions what it lost.

That is correct **for its actual job** — detecting a finding declared both open and closed — but its printed line `declared open : N` is read by fires as *the number of open findings*, and it is not: **a finding filed with 🔴, 🟠 or 🔵 is counted as neither open nor closed.** ✓ **Measured this fire, not inferred** (`logs/session-scratch/s1318-census-reconcile.mjs`, diffing the ID sets across `57b9d9bb..HEAD` rather than trusting the totals): **F-1316-1 sat as a 🔴 row and was NOT COUNTED AT ALL** the whole time it was the board’s top player-facing defect; two of the three findings I filed today (🟠 F-1318-1, 🔵 F-1318-2/3) are likewise invisible. Eight saturated children cannot be absent from a CPU-sorted list. **The children had already exited: a timing failure, not a filter failure.** ⚠️ **SCOPE — THIS NARROWS s1273's §E2, WHICH SAID LEAVING IT BROKEN "POISONS AN OWNER-GATED DECISION".** It does not. F-1270-4 states its confirming test in **throughput multipliers** (*"~7–12× confirms the mechanism, ~3× refutes it"*), and those come from `runN()`'s hrtime around child exit — **a separate and sound path**. What changed: the delay is **derived from the median 8-child time this machine just measured** (`fraction 0.5`, compensated for top's own second-sample latency) instead of a constant; the run records `topInvokedAtMs` / `topReturnedAtMs` / `topLatencyMs` / `childrenAliveAtTopInvoke` / `childrenAliveAtTopReturn` so the label is **falsifiable by the reader**; and **the label is earned or withheld** — a reading with zero child rows is marked `INVALID … Do NOT read idlePercent as arm load` and never called "during". An arm too short to contain a valid sample is **skipped and said so** — *an unsampled arm reports nothing, not idle*. 🧪 **BOTH DIRECTIONS EXERCISED:** **fire arm, real run** → `IN-ARM: 8 child row(s) observed, 8/8 still alive when top returned`, idle 44.12%, children ~63.4% each (v2's blind luck on the long arm is now v3's guarantee) · **short-arm mutant** (a copy with the workload cut 9e8→3e7, v3 itself untouched) → 8-child arm **0.18 s** → `observation: SKIPPED — arm ~0.18s is too short … NO SAMPLE TAKEN`, where v2 would have slept 3500 ms and printed an idle number. ⓘ **Stated honestly: the third branch (children die *while* top runs → `INVALID`) is a defensive backstop and was NOT exercised** — with the 0.5 fraction and the 300 ms floor the schedule avoids that regime by construction, so it only fires if load shifts between the reps and the observation.

🔻 **F-1256-3 (s1256, MEASURED — SMALL, CHEAP, AND IT BIT ME TWICE IN ONE FIRE).** `scripts/citation-title-guard.mjs` scans **tracked** `.md` only, so **a newly authored master's citations are invisible to it until the authoring commit lands** — which is exactly one step too late, because the house pattern is *run the guards, then commit*. Measured here by accident: the guard reported **PASS, 310 scanned** with my new master sitting untracked in the tree, then **FAIL** on that same file's `e2e/helpers/hero-approach.ts:5` (`export async function moveHeroTo(page: Page, x: number, z: number): Promise<void> {`; inlined in `e2e/release-build.spec.ts` until `af48a749` retired the duplicate — pointer repaired s1259, the claim below is unchanged) the moment `47f5f0aa` made it tracked (`found 2`). Both citations were bare the whole time; only the guard's visibility changed. **Consequence: every fire that authors a master and gates before committing gets a free false green**, and the failure only surfaces on some later fire's unrelated run — where it looks like that fire's fault. Not urgent (the guard does catch it eventually, and it caught mine), but the fix is small: scan the working tree, or have the authoring path re-run the guard after `git add`. Until then, **authoring fires should run `test:citations` a second time after the commit** — this fire did, which is the only reason its own master is clean.

✅ **F-1280-1 (s1280, FOUND + FOLDED INTO THE MASTER — THE HANDOFF'S EDIT PLAN NAMED THE ADVERTISEMENT AND MISSED THE ENFORCER).** s1279 §I.1 specified the rung-conformance scope as *"`auto_pan` 3→2, `place_building` 3 declared, the spec ladder line amended"* and named exactly one code file, `src/agent/ToolSurface.ts`. ✅ **F-1251-2 (s1251, MEASURED + FIXED THIS FIRE) — THE SOLE GATE OVER THE E1 RELEASE DOOR PRINTED AN AFFIRMATIVE ALL-CLEAR OVER A SUBJECT IT HAD NEVER READ, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT F-1126-1's STANDING REMEDY WOULD HAVE BUILT.** 🎯 **The act was "ATTEMPT the repeated ask, don't restate it."** F-1126-1 has ridden the desk for many fires asking that the guards be wired into a gate; before wiring anything you must know what the guard does when a gate calls it. **Measured (`logs/session-scratch/s1251/armD-empty-dist.txt`): run `scripts/assert-release-build.mjs` with `GR_RELEASE=e1` from a cwd with no `dist/` and it prints `[release-build] E1-only: 0 files, 0 bytes, zero later manifest ids or plate/GLB assets` and EXITS 0.** 🔑 **The mechanism is one line:** `walk()` swallows a missing directory (`readdir(...).catch(() => [])`), so `files` is `[]`, every check below iterates nothing, and the summary sentence asserts a cleanliness nobody verified. **This is the F-1104-7 / F-1250-1 shape a third time in a different file — an affirmative verdict about a thing that was never examined — and here it is aimed at the release door.** The failure scenario is not hypothetical: the remedy being asked for is a bare `node scripts/assert-release-build.mjs` in a battery, and `scripts/deploy.sh` runs `npm run build`, *not* `build:release`, so nothing on the deploy path guarantees a release `dist/` exists when the guard runs. 🔬 **THE SAME CLASS ONE LAYER DOWN, FOUND BY ASKING WHAT ELSE THIS GUARD BUILDS AT RUNTIME.** The plate/GLB leak check is only as strong as `laterAssetStems`, a blacklist **rebuilt from disk on every run** by walking `assets/raw` and `assets/pilots/map-rebuild-spike`. **Measured today: 261 stems (36 plate-contract + 225 .glb) — so it is NOT vacuous now, and I say so rather than dressing a latent hole as a live one.** But if those dirs are ever moved or renamed — a routine reorganisation, not a disaster — the set empties and both leak checks pass silently. ✅ **F-1249-1 (s1249, MEASURED + FIXED THIS FIRE) — THE REFUSAL s1248 SHIPPED COULD NOT STATE ITS CAUSE ON 3 OF THE 15 LEAVES IT REFUSES, AND THE SENTENCE IT PRINTED INSTEAD WAS A FALSE CLAIM ABOUT TWO FILES IT NEVER OPENS — WHICH IS EXACTLY HOW MY PREDECESSOR CAME TO ESCALATE A FALSE ALARM ABOUT THE OWNER'S MONEY.** 🎯 **PROVENANCE — this fire opened by REFUTING the lead it inherited, and the refutation is what found the defect.** s1248's handoff (I) flagged as UNVERIFIED that `autosprite-trial-gate` shows `superseded` while F-1173-7 had registered it **`blocked`** with the gate *"OWNER-GATED ON CREDITS — NOT FIRE-QUEUEABLE … IT SPENDS MONEY, which CLAUDE.md §7.3 reserves for the owner absolutely"*, and warned *"a money-gated item has been quietly moved off Robin's desk."* ✅ **REFUTED AT SOURCE: the retirement WAS an owner ruling.** `ce41d476` (2026-07-29 07:31) flipped the leaf quoting the owner **verbatim** — *"this can be canned - we don't need that"* — and the same ruling is recorded in `tasks/BACKLOG.md:1805` **and** the master-retirement commit `c84306ad`. **No credits were ever spent; nothing left Robin's desk that he did not himself close.** 🚨 **BUT WHY DID s1248 BELIEVE OTHERWISE? BECAUSE THE GUARD IT HAD JUST FIXED TOLD IT NOTHING.** Run on that leaf, `drain-block-check` printed **`(no reason recorded on the leaf — the why lives only in BACKLOG/reviews)`** — over an object whose **`title`, one field away, carries the owner's verbatim canning and its date**, and whose stale **`blockedReason` still read "Lifted by the OWNER only, never by a green battery."** The guard's silence corroborated the alarm. 🔬 **THE DEFECT, AND IT IS THE SAME CLASS ONE FIRE LATER IN THE SAME FILE:** F-1248-1 fixed the drain path's *status* vocabulary and then shipped a *reason* vocabulary with the identical narrowness. `closedReason()` matched six exact keys plus one adhoc pattern — `/^(stopped|stop|closed)Note/i` — which is anchored to the **suffix stem of the single session-stamped spelling s1248 happened to hold** (`stoppedNote_s1216`) and misses every sibling that varies the **stem**: `supersededNote_s1116`, `drainNote_s1170`, `note_s1170`. 📊 **MEASURED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING — AND MY FIRST INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE POINT.** I first re-implemented the lookup and got **5 of 15**; that model did not know about the adhoc arm at `:67`, so I threw it away and ran the **real script** against all 15 terminal-closed leaves. (3) The **`leaf title` now prints UNCONDITIONALLY on both refusal arms** — §4.7 puts an owner's verbatim ruling in the title, so on a canned leaf the title IS the cause and any reason key is secondary bookkeeping, which is precisely how autosprite read (`note_s1174: Verified at source this fire` over an owner canning). This fire is the fourth turn of the same screw, and the subject was the previous fire's own cure.** Two lessons worth keeping. **(a) A guard that refuses without being able to say WHY does not merely inconvenience the next fire — it manufactures false beliefs, and I can name the cost: an escalation about the owner's money, written by a careful fire, caused by a printed sentence.** **(b) When you re-derive someone's measurement, run THEIR instrument, not your model of it.** My reimplementation of a 12-line function was already wrong by 40% (5 vs 3) because it did not know about a branch seven lines below the one I was reading.* — one rider left open, UNVERIFIED and harmless: `lane-calibrate-suite-workers.md` resolves to the **blocked v2** leaf rather than to its own superseded leaf (the matcher's longest-substring tie-break shadows it), so that leaf is unreachable by its own taskFile. rc=1 either way and the stricter refusal wins, so it is a curiosity, not a hole.

✅ **F-1247-1 (s1247, MEASURED + FIXED THIS FIRE, `e66af39d`) — THE GATE BATTERY'S OWN SELECTOR COULD REPORT A GREEN OVER A BATTERY IT SILENTLY NARROWED, AND IT IS THE EXACT SHAPE THE FILE REFUSES TWICE IN ITS OWN COMMENTS.** `scripts/run-guards.mjs:158` built its changed-file set as `` `${diff.stdout}\n${untracked.status === 0 ? untracked.stdout : ''}` `` — so **any** failure of `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` contributed an **empty string** instead of stopping. ⚠️ **This is the same failure-as-absence class as F-1246-1, and s1246's scope sweep could not have found it:** that sweep hunted the `try/catch → ''` shape, and **`spawnSync` never throws** — the conversion here is a **ternary on `status === 0`**, invisible to a catch-pattern grep. 🔬 **PROVED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING, with the single variable isolated.** A PATH shim failed *only* `ls-files --others` and passed every other git call through. ✅ STRUCK s1345 (closure row at head of ledger) — **F-1298-2 (s1298, RAISED BY CODE READ — A CRASHED GR-SIM WILL REPORT AN OPAQUE asyncio ERROR INSTEAD OF THE DIAGNOSTIC THE CODE CAREFULLY BUILT.)** `env/goldrush-verifiers/goldrush/__init__.py`, `_read_sim_reply` races a stdout and a stderr `readline()` and picks whichever lands first. **The uncovered case: stdout completes but is EMPTY** (EOF — GR-SIM crashed or exited without emitting a view) **while the stderr task is still pending.** Control then falls through to `await process.stderr.read()` *while `stderr_task` is still awaiting a readline on that same `StreamReader`*, and asyncio raises `RuntimeError: read() called while another coroutine is already waiting for incoming data`. Fire-authorable, one function** — cancel-and-await `stderr_task` on every exit path, or read the remainder from the completed task rather than re-reading the stream.

Sweeping the depth: limit **10 → 13 from end (visible)**, **14 → 17 (visible)**, **16 → 19 (visible)**, **18 → 21 (LOST)**, **25 → 28 (LOST)**. **The window only truncates at `stackTraceLimit ≥ 18`, and the default is 10 — seven frames of headroom.** So for an ordinary uncaught throw the runner *does* show the diagnosis, and the lost cause must be explained by something else: a non-Error termination (signal/OOM, which prints a much longer V8 trace — note `:209` already handles `status === null` as `signal:<sig>`), output arriving *after* the crash, or the original observation being a loose description of the tail. ➡️ **NEXT STEP IF ANYONE PICKS THIS UP:** do not "fix" the window — capture the *whole* failing output once (the runner already holds it in `row.output`; only the print is windowed) and wait for the next natural red, rather than authoring a corrective against an unproven cause. **No corrective authored, deliberately: there is no proven defect here, and s1241 declined to invent one.**

⚡ **"GUARDS 8/8" IS A COIN FLIP WHENEVER A LANE IS RUNNING — `test:power-budget` reds 20–33% of the time on a working box, and the distribution says it is PREEMPTION, not a regression (F-1160-2, s1160 2026-07-28, MEASURED n=20 — small fire-authorable corrective, not an owner call).** ✓ Not a flake dismissal and not inherited: s1160 ran the full battery twice in four minutes and got **8/8 then 7/8 then 8/8**, which is worth nothing on its own — so it measured the RATE. `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-power-graph-budget.mjs`, **n=20 back-to-back: 4 over cap (20%)**; an independent n=12 earlier in the same fire gave **4 fail (33%)**. 🔑 **The distribution is BIMODAL with a clean gap, which is the whole diagnosis:** sixteen runs cluster **0.368–0.496 ms** (median **0.416**, ~17% under the 0.500 ms cap) and then it jumps straight to **0.631 / 0.658 / 0.725 / 0.899** — *nothing between 0.496 and 0.631*. **A cap set too tight produces values straddling it continuously; a scheduler steal produces exactly this gap.** ✓ Cause verified at source, not guessed: `scripts/check-power-graph-budget.mjs:35-43` asserts the **p95 of `diagnostics().lastStepMs`** — a pure wall-clock CPU measurement with no I/O — against `POWER_GRAPH_LIMITS.solveBudgetMs`, taken from **one** run of 160 samples. Box at the time: **loadavg ~6.9–7.6 of 16 cores**, carrying lane-d's 2396-test playwright suite plus two live wrangler dev servers. **So the guard is measuring the factory, not the game.** ⚠️ **WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING:** the battery is the one s1146 proved had been *red for a day while nobody ran it* and s1159 fought back to 8/8 — **a guard that reds at random is how a battery gets trained-out**, and every fire that writes "guards 8/8" in a handoff is reporting a **sample**, not a state (mine included; the claim in s1160's line-1 is annotated accordingly). ➡️ **RECOMMENDATION (a): take the MINIMUM p95 across 3 repeats inside the script.** The minimum is the least-preempted sample, so it measures the code's real cost; a genuine regression lifts the floor and still trips the gate, while scheduler noise — which only ever *adds* time — is removed by construction. Median body 0.416 leaves ~20% headroom, so the cap itself needs no loosening and **must not be loosened** (that would be the F-1156-2 mistake in a new costume). (b) require a quiet box — rejected: unenforceable, the factory is never quiet by design. **GATE for whoever takes it: re-run the old script n≥20 BEFORE editing (this line is that baseline), then n≥20 after, on a comparably loaded box — the fix is proven by the over-cap count going 4/20 → 0/20 with the median unmoved, not by one green run.** ✅ **RE-DERIVED s1161 BEFORE ANYONE ACTS ON IT — the remedy survives, one third of the diagnosis does not, and the RATE is not a property of the guard.** Per this board’s own law (a finding’s recommendation is an untested second hypothesis), I re-measured rather than authoring the fix off s1160’s numbers. Instrument: `logs/session-scratch/s1161-power-budget-rate.mjs`, two arms **interleaved** (order is a confound), n=12 each, on a box carrying lane-d’s 2396-test suite + two wrangler servers (loadavg **6.91/16**). **(1) THE RATE IS LOAD-DEPENDENT, SO “20%” IS NOT A CONSTANT:** default-QoS came back **1/12 over cap (8%)**, not 20–33%, and the body was far tighter than s1160’s — **0.338–0.371, median 0.346** vs its 0.368–0.496/median 0.416, with a single outlier at **0.529**. Same script, same cap, different hour: the number measures the BOX, not the code. Quote the rate with its load or not at all. **(2) THE “SCHEDULER STEAL” LABEL IS RIGHT IN KIND — and I tried to refute it with a specific mechanism, which FAILED, and that is worth recording.** Hypothesis: Apple-Silicon E-core scheduling, which would explain a clean bimodal gap that continuous contention would not. Control: the same guard under `taskpolicy -b` (background QoS). Result: **12/12 over cap at 1.628–1.846 ms — a ~5× slowdown, not the 1.8–2.6× s1160 observed.** So **pure E-core placement is NOT the slow mode**; the real shape is a MIXTURE — some fraction of the 160 samples served slow — which also explains why p95 (`samples[151]`, the 152nd of 160) needs **≥9** degraded samples to move at all, i.e. a sustained stall, never a single blip. **(3) THE RECOMMENDATION HOLDS, WITH A LIMIT NOBODY HAD STATED:** min-of-3 over consecutive triples scored **0/4 over cap in the default arm** — it works — but **4/4 in the background-QoS arm**. **min-of-3 cures transient steal and CANNOT rescue a systematically deprioritised process**, so it must not be sold as a general cure. ➡️ **Therefore the stronger fix, and it is this repo’s own instrument-control idiom (the one that blocked E7 attempt 1): measure a fixed known-cost reference loop in the SAME process and report it.** If the reference is also degraded, the honest verdict is **“environment degraded”**, not “PowerGraph regressed” — which is the actual defect here, since the guard currently blames the code for the box. ⛔ Still do **NOT** loosen the cap. **The n=20 baseline above plus this n=12 two-arm control are jointly the gate for proving any fix.**

But the runner was live (I had just queued lane-c attempt 2 to it) and `fire-runner.sh` is the script that **was executing this very fire**, so "wait for idle" had no window at all for two of the three. **Resolved with an atomic-rename swap instead of an in-place edit:** copy to an in-repo temp (same filesystem, so `mv` is a true `rename(2)`), edit the temp, `mv` it over the original — the running `bash` keeps its file descriptor on the **old inode** and finishes the version it started with, while the new version takes effect at the next fresh invocation. **Zero risk, no waiting, and it honours the law's intent (never corrupt a running runner) rather than only its letter.** Verified after each swap: both runner pids still alive, `tasks/running/` still holding the live lane-c task, `fire-runner.sh` tail intact through `exit 0`, file modes preserved (v3 `-rw-r--r--`, fire-runner `-rwxr-xr-x` — the exec bit survived). Diffs are comment-only replacements of a single command line, which bash never tokenizes, so the unavailability of `bash -n` (permission-gated for fires) cost no assurance. **Consequence to state plainly: `tasks/runs/` and `logs/fire-*.log` now grow without bound.** That is the intended trade — the owner ruled *"our history is our strength"*, and s1031 measured a real casualty (a 886,731-token run log already silently gone). The disk answer is **F-1027-2, still one word on the owner's desk ("tails" or "gzip")**, and it is now the only thing standing between the factory and unbounded log growth — **it just became the more urgent of his open questions.**

## s1072 (2026-07-26, fire) — THE UNOWNED ONBOARDING RED HAS A ROOT CAUSE, AND IT IS A SPAWN POINT THAT MOVED TWO UNITS SEVEN DAYS AGO

- 🎯 **THE MECHANISM: the greeter is chosen by PROXIMITY between exactly two candidates, and the player's spawn point moved across the midpoint.** `TownScene.firstClaimGreeter()` (`src/town/TownScene.ts:1293-1307`) iterates the roster and **skips every actor except `tavernkeeper` and `elder`**, returning whichever is nearest the hero — with no bark-radius gate, so it always returns one of the two. **`d1f549d5` (2026-07-19, `runner(lane-a): lane-landmark-collision.md`) changed `HERO_START` from `(0, 0.06, 0)` to `(0, 0.06, 2)`** — a two-unit shift made to fix a landmark collision, which crossed the midpoint between Marta Vale and Elder Rowan and **silently reassigned the onboarding greeting**. Distances computed both ways, and the flip is robust in both coordinate systems: at **z=0** Marta 8.64 / Rowan 9.91 ⇒ **Marta greets**; at **z=2** Marta 10.28 / Rowan 8.53 ⇒ **Rowan greets** (definition coords) — and at the plaza-placed RUNTIME coords the same flip holds (z=0: Marta 8.11 / Rowan 9.50; z=2: Marta 9.44 / Rowan 8.53).
- 🧾 **THREE CANDIDATE EXPLANATIONS WERE KILLED BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE RIGHT ONE SURVIVED, and each kill is worth recording.** **(1) "the town layout drifted"** — FALSE: both actors' `position` literals in `src/town/townsfolk.ts` are **byte-identical at every commit** from `0aace826` through HEAD. **(2) "the roster gating changed and the elder appeared"** — FALSE: `requiresBuilding` is **absent on both** at every one of those commits (it gates only `storekeeper`/`preacher`), so both have always been visible. **(3) "the townsfolk walk, so the winner is racy"** — FALSE: `TownActorRuntime.position` *is* live (`:2267`) and *is* time-driven for looping actors (`:2299`), but **`loop` is absent on both greeter candidates** (only `youngster_a`/`youngster_b`/`newsie`/`prospector` walk), so the selection is deterministic, not flaky.
- ⚠️ **METHOD WARNING, paid for in this fire: a `-S` pickaxe that says "never changed" is not evidence about a value that changed inside an unchanged line.** `git log -S "HERO_START = new THREE.Vector3"` reported **only** the 2026-07-07 creation and appeared to exonerate the spawn outright — because the pickaxe reports commits where the **count** of a string changes, and that literal occurs exactly once before and after. **`-G` (regex) found `d1f549d5` immediately.** The false exoneration cost most of an investigation and nearly shipped "cause unknown."
- ⚖️ **WHICH SIDE IS WRONG — the ENGINE IS COHERENT AND THE ASSERTION OVER-SPECIFIES, but the flip was an ACCIDENT, and those two facts point at different fixes.** For the engine: the two-candidate whitelist is deliberate and **unchanged since the feature shipped**, and the greeting line itself — `FIRST_CLAIM_GREETING` (`:111`) = *"The valley's open. **The tavern keeps the contracts.** Go stake your first claim."* — is written in the **third person about the tavern**, which reads correctly from the schoolhouse elder and distinctly oddly from the tavernkeeper standing inside her own tavern. The guide trail still targets the tavernkeeper (`:1240`), so the chain *elder greets → trail → tavern → board → launch* is coherent. Against: `d1f549d5` was a **landmark-collision fix** with no stated intent to touch onboarding, so today's greeter is **accidental, not designed** — and relaxing the test would bless an accident. **The spec has been modified exactly once, at its introduction, so the assertion is original and was correct on the day it was written.**

🔴 **F-1081-10 — THE DEPLOY FAILURE IS A REPRODUCIBLE *TRANSPORT* FAILURE, NOT AUTH AND NOT SIZE. THE STANDING DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG, AND THIS NOW BLOCKS SIX MERGED GAMEPLAY CHANGES.** ✓ VERIFIED s1081 by running `bash scripts/deploy.sh` **twice** and reading the wrangler log both times — the first fresh attempt since s1078, because re-running a known-failing command is only pointless if you don't read the log. Both attempts fail identically at `pages deploy`, exit 0 (the script never blocks, as designed), with `✘ Failed to upload files. Please try again. Error: {}` — an **empty** error object, which is why this has been mis-attributed. The log tells the real story: repeated `TypeError: fetch failed` whose `[cause]` is **`Error: write EPIPE`** and **`SocketError: other side closed`**, across many parallel upload connections, fatal after ~30 s.

**What this rules OUT, with evidence:**
- **NOT auth** — zero `401`/`403`/`token`/`scope` anywhere in the log; wrangler authenticates and reaches the API fine.
- **NOT quota/rate** — no `429`.
- **NOT the ~118 MB size theory** (s1078's premise): the script's own budget check **passes with room to spare** — `16,480,199 bytes` against the cap, **8,519,801 bytes of headroom**, on both desktop and mobile.
- **NOT a one-off transient** — the retry reproduced it exactly, so "Please try again" is not the answer either. (And bandwidth is not the constraint: F-1076-1 measured a **184.9 MB** git push completing in **65 s** on this machine.)

**What it points AT:** the connection is being closed mid-write by the far side, repeatedly, under wrangler's *parallel* upload fan-out. Candidate causes worth one owner-side look each: wrangler 4.107.0's upload concurrency against this network path (a proxy, a router, or an ISP dropping many simultaneous long-lived POSTs), or a Cloudflare-side per-connection limit. ➡️ **CHEAP THINGS TO TRY BEFORE ANY BIG DECISION:** (a) a concurrency/`--no-bundle`-style throttle on the Pages upload, (b) the same deploy from a different network, (c) a wrangler version change. **`scripts/deploy.sh` also has no retry and no upload-concurrency control at all** — adding both is small, fire-authorable, and testable only by an owner-present run.
⚠️ **This supersedes the framing of F-1051-3 "option (2)".** The owner may have been offered the wrong choice: the blocker looks like a fixable transport setting, not something requiring the option-(2) tradeoff. **Six merged gameplay changes are now unplayable by the family** (`d2279d32`, `5bad5def`, `5b61349e`, `52fa15ad`, `29625771`, and today's `eb7278ac` + `925a0c3b`), which makes this the highest-value owner item on the desk.

### s1128 — F-1126-2 RE-EXAMINED: its factual half is true, its implied remedy is WRONG and would un-ship T2–T10 (2026-07-27)
- ✅ **F-1126-2's FACTUAL HALF RE-VERIFIED, not inherited: `test:release` has no caller.** Tree-wide grep (excluding `node_modules`/`.git`/`logs`/`tasks`) returns exactly three hits — its own definition at `package.json:25`, and prose in `STATUS.md` + `reviews/e1-release-build-measured.md`. There is no `.github/workflows`, and `scripts/deploy.sh` never mentions it. **0 callers: confirmed.**
- 🔴 **BUT THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM IT — "so no release suite gates a deploy", implying the fix is to wire it in — IS FALSE AND ACTIVELY DANGEROUS. `test:release` validates a DIFFERENT BUILD than the one deployed.** `scripts/deploy.sh:49` publishes `npm run build` = **all-epoch**. `test:release` (`playwright.release.config.ts`) validates `GR_RELEASE=e1 npm run build:release` = **E1-only**, and its assertions demand the *absence* of later content: `e2e/release-build.spec.ts:165` asserts `e7-relay-valley`/`e10-last-claim` **decline to the Claim**, and `:195` asserts dist has **no later manifest ids or plate/GLB assets**.
- 📏 **PROVEN, not read off: running that suite's own dist assertion against the artifact deploy.sh actually publishes exits 1.** Probe `logs/_s1128_release_assert_probe.mjs` (read-only; `assert-release-build.mjs` only `readdir`/`readFile`/`stat`) → **`rc=1`, `[release-build] later epoch manifest id in assets/Game-LdGRoKUW-diet-576343bc.js`**. Current `dist/` is genuinely the deployed shape: **406 GLBs**, later-epoch ids present. So the suite is not merely unwired — **it is incompatible with the deploy by construction.**
- ☢️ **AND THE NAIVE WIRING IS WORSE THAN A NO-OP — IT WOULD SILENTLY SHIP A DIFFERENT GAME.** `playwright.release.config.ts` sets `reuseExistingServer: false` and a `webServer.command` of `GR_RELEASE=e1 npm run build:release && vite preview`, so **every invocation of `npm run test:release` overwrites `dist/` with an E1-only build.** Dropping it into `deploy.sh` between the build (`:49`) and the snapshot (`cp -R dist/.`, `:80`) would publish a build with **T2–T10 stripped** — content the owner deliberately kept (s1056: E1-only measured at −350 MiB but **"DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED — product call"**). This is Mistake #14's shape: the vocabulary can't express the fix, so **reject-don't-stretch**. ➡️ **RULING FOR THE NEXT FIRE/ATTENDED: do NOT wire `test:release` into the deploy path. Its 0 refs are CORRECT** — it is an option-measuring instrument for an un-taken owner decision, not an orphaned guard. Standing operational trap worth knowing: **any fire that runs `npm run test:release` leaves `dist/` E1-only** (s1056 hit this and restored it by hand); `deploy.sh` self-protects only because it rebuilds at `:49` first.
- 🔴 **F-1128-1 — THE REAL GAP F-1126-2 WAS REACHING FOR, CORRECTLY AIMED: the deploy already runs a genuine boot assertion and then THROWS ITS VERDICT AWAY in the mode the DEPLOY LAW uses.** `deploy.sh:59-64` runs `asset-diet.spec.ts --grep "honest town and claim cues"`, which really does prove the game boots — it polls `#game-canvas[data-asset-loading-state]` to **`ready`** with a 45 s timeout (`e2e/asset-diet.spec.ts:96`) and asserts the raising-cue appears then hides (`:93-97`). **But `:74-77` collapses two unlike failures into one advisory branch** — `BUDGET_RC != 0` (*the boot check failed*) and `BUDGET_OVER != 0` (*merely over 25 MB*) — and in default mode both only `WARN: asset budget check failed — default mode continues`, after which the snapshot publishes. `STRICT=0` unless `--strict` (`:8-9`), and the DEPLOY LAW has fires invoke plain `bash scripts/deploy.sh`. **Net: the only gate that can block a publish is compile-and-bundle (`npm run build` = tsc + vite + asset-diet.mjs, which aborts at `:49`). Zero behavioural assertions can stop a bad build reaching the family.**
- ℹ️ **HONESTLY BOUNDED, so this is not oversold: the practical risk is real but partly mitigated.** Deployed code is main, which passed a drain gate — though s1126's F-1126-1 showed that gate is itself only `tsc` + `build` (`.claude/skills/drain/SKILL.md:28-29`), so the mitigation is thinner than it sounds. Also checked before claiming a gap: `scripts/test-deploy-contract.sh` does **not** contract this behaviour either way — all 9 cases run `--strict` and none exercises `budget_failed` (code 5), so the default-mode advisory path is **untested**, not deliberately ratified. Note the file header's "Never blocks anything" (`:3-4`) is about **exit codes** (fires never get blocked), which is a separate axis from **what may publish**.

## s1455 (2026-08-04, fire) — A HOLD VERDICT HAS NO ENFORCEMENT SURFACE, AND NOW IT HAS A GUARD

- 🛠️ **F-1455-1 — THE STALE-HOLD-VERDICT CLASS IS MECHANIZED: `scripts/stale-hold-verdict-guard.test.mjs`, rooted in `test:ledger-guards` (12 guards now — COUNT it, never prune it).** s1454 found the class by hand — a review whose `## VERDICT` still refuses the merge while its goal leaf says the slice shipped — bannered three rows and *recommended* a guard rather than building one at fire-end (F-1300-4: a fire mutates gate topology late and then cannot see it). This fire had a drain-dry board and built it at fire START, with the full battery as the last act. ⚖️ **The class is real and it is BIGGER than the hand sweep found: s1455 re-derived it independently and caught TWO MORE that a sample of nine had missed.** (1) `reviews/gg-03-gazette-panel-swap.md` said **⛔ BLOCKED — do not merge** while the panel swap has been live on main since 2026-07-29 — `src/news/heraldReader.ts:177` carries the exact `<img class="claim-herald__art-slot" data-testid="gazette-panel-engraving">` it describes, discharged by the GG-03c ladder at `b5be7ab3`. ⚠️ **That commit is headlined** *"fix: goals.json schema — two violations turned test:node-guards red on main (F-1211-2)"* **and in fact carries six `gazette-panel-*.webp` plates plus the herald engravings — a headline names intent, `--stat` names content.** (2) `reviews/m2-05-geometry-settle.md` said **"The leaf does NOT close"**; the leaf closed at `99bd76fd` *"s1040: drain m2-05-geometry-settle — F-1035-1 geometry race CLOSED by a stability wait, proved twice over"*, **fifteen fires earlier**, verified by ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 99bd76fd main` rc=0) and never by the leaf status field. Its done-move sits in `tasks/failed/` as `shipped-s1064-99bd76fd.md` — a `shipped-` prefix inside `failed/`, the shape that makes this class invisible to a directory-level sweep. Both now carry supersede banners with the original verdicts KEPT verbatim (retention law).
- ⚠️ **AND THE REUSABLE HALF IS THAT THE CLASSIFIER, NOT THE LOOKUP, IS THE HARD PART — MY OWN FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG IN EXACTLY THE WAY THE LESSON WARNS (a fresh classifier's first hits are probably its own bug).** Matching `HOLD|HELD|NOT MERGED|WITHHELD|BLOCKED` anywhere in the verdict LINE produced six hits of which **four were the instrument, not the board**: `e2-rail-tough-only-bind` (*"MERGE — the firewall **held** byte-for-byte"*), `f1420-1` (*"MERGE — gates green, scope 4's STOP condition **held**"*), `eight-winds-e2-row-order-survey` (*"**ACCEPTED** — the wiring slice stays **blocked**"*) and `art-e7-town-icons` (*"QA PASS — reference-tier, extraction **WITHHELD**"*). Every one is a MERGE verdict whose prose happens to discuss holding — **which is what review prose is about.** A guard reddening on those trains fires to ignore it, which is worse than no guard. ➡️ **The guard therefore classifies on the DECISION TOKEN ONLY** — the span before the first em-dash, period or comma — and all four false positives are pinned as fixtures so the sentence form cannot creep back. ⓘ **Lookup needed three keys, also measured rather than assumed:** of 13 mappable refusals, **6 resolved by file stem, 4 by `taskFile`, 3 by the Slice header**. `gg-03` is the instructive one — **its leaf id names the BLOCKED slice while its `taskFile` names the SUCCESSOR that discharged it**, so a `taskFile`-only lookup would never have found the stale row it was built to find.
- ✅ **PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING THE DEFECT, NOT BY A GREEN (the s1299/s1300 standard) — a passing guard never executes its violation path.** `artifacts/s1455/manufacture-defect.mjs` copies the full 683-file reviews corpus to `/tmp` (**never into main's working tree — §3.0b custody, and two lanes were live**), strips one supersede banner, and runs the guard against it: **rc=1 both times**, naming exactly one offender each time, with the corpus-size assertions still GREEN — so the red is attributable to the manufactured defect rather than to a shrunken corpus. Both banners are therefore proven **load-bearing**. ⓘ The guard's paths are env-redirectable **only** so this probe can run outside main's tree; the redirect **cannot silence it** — the instrument-validation test asserts a large corpus, so pointing it anywhere small REDS rather than greens. **Unmapped refusals (4) are REPORTED, never red**: an unmatched review is F-1448-6 leaf debt, a different finding with a different owner. **GATE: closed — the guard is rooted, its red path is proven, and the two stale rows it found are bannered.**
